---
title: "How this was verified"
subtitle: "Provenance, audit protocol, and what the verdicts do and do not mean"
---

## Where this material came from

This catalog is derived from a deep-research document produced by a large language model
(ChatGPT deep research) in July 2026, covering open methodological, theoretical, practical,
data-related and interpretive problems in target trial emulation.

That origin is the reason this page exists. A machine-generated research agenda is a
plausible-sounding artifact whether or not it is correct, and publishing one as settled fact
would be a disservice. **Nothing from the source document appears on this site without a
verification verdict attached**, and the evidence behind each verdict is shown on the entry
itself.

The source document is kept as working material and is not published here.

### One thing worth recording about the source

The source was supplied in three formats. **The markdown export had lost every citation.**
ChatGPT's markdown export replaces each link with private-use-area characters and an opaque
handle, so the exported file contained 125 citation tokens, zero DOIs, zero URLs, and zero
PubMed identifiers. The `.docx` of the same document retained the real hyperlinks.

Extraction therefore runs from the `.docx`, not the export. That distinction is not cosmetic: had
the markdown been used, every entry in this catalog would have been unsourced, and the audit
would have had nothing to check a citation against.

## What was checked mechanically

Before any of the substantive audit, every resolvable identifier in the source was checked
against its registry.

The source carries 48 numbered references pointing at 35 distinct works.

| Outcome | Count | What it means |
|---|---:|---|
| Resolved to a real work | 21 | Identifier and title confirmed against CrossRef, NCBI or arXiv |
| Guidance or software | 7 | Regulatory guidance, reporting standards and package documentation, correctly cited by URL |
| Unresolved | 7 | The publisher page blocks automated access, and no search result matched the prose context closely enough to record |

The seven unresolved references are listed with `"confidence": "none"` in the working files and
**are not cited anywhere in this catalog**. A reference that cannot be confirmed is left out
rather than guessed at; an invented citation would discredit every other entry here.

## The audit

Every problem carries a set of atomic, falsifiable claims extracted from the source. Those
claims, not the prose around them, are what was tested.

### Literature verification

For each problem, every cited work was checked to confirm it supports the claim attributed to
it, and the screened corpus on this site was searched for later work that would resolve or
narrow the problem. The search ran against the 1,376 records held locally rather than against
recall, so every locator in a verification opinion is a record that exists in the collection and
can be opened. Where the search found nothing, the opinion says so and its confidence is capped,
because absence from one corpus of PubMed and PMC records is weak evidence of absence in the
field.

### Adversarial refutation

The adversarial lens is one of the independent auditors rather than a separate pass. It is given
an inverted prior: assume the problem has already been solved, and go find who solved it. Asking
a model to confirm a claim and asking it to break the claim produce different results, and only
the second is informative.

The sibling project this pipeline was ported from declares a separate refuting auditor in its
adjudication rule that casts no opinions, which leaves one guard in that rule permanently inert.
Rather than reproduce a lens that is named and does not run, the roster here names only auditors
that vote, and the rule counts only those.

### Independent external auditors

Frontier models outside this system were given the same claims, blind to each other and to the
literature pass, each with a different lens:

- a **technical and source-code lens**, which checks identification arguments, weight algebra,
  cloning and censoring bookkeeping, and immortal-time accounting, and which verifies any claim
  about a software package against that package's pinned source rather than against the report;
- a **recency and prior-art lens**, which adopts an inverted prior. It assumes each problem has
  already been solved and goes looking for who solved it, because an agenda that lists a solved
  problem as open is the most damaging error this site can make: the people most likely to read
  it are the people who solved it;
- a **third independent lens** on the same claims, so that a majority is a majority of more than
  two.

Each entry's page lists the auditors that voted on it. Coverage is not uniform. External models
run out of quota mid-run, and one of them intermittently returns a well-formed but empty verdict
for a batch, answering in about a hundred tokens where a real assessment takes several thousand.
Those batches are detected and re-run rather than counted as complete, and the ones that stay
empty after a re-run leave the entry adjudicated by fewer auditors. Where that happened the page
says so, rather than presenting a thinner audit as an equal one, and every majority rule is
taken over the auditors that actually voted on that entry.

### Adjudication

Opinions become a published verdict by a fixed rule, not by judgment. The rule records its own
decision path on every entry, so the route from votes to verdict is visible.

Two principles govern it:

**A "solved" vote without a locator is not evidence.** It is downgraded rather than counted. An
auditor asserting that something has been solved must name the work that solved it.

**Evidence beats votes.** A lone dissenter holding an unrebutted verbatim quote is not silently
outvoted by auditors holding opinions.

Majority rules carry a denominator. A verdict such as
[Overstated]{.verdict .verdict-overstated} requires at least two independent auditors and at
least half of the auditors that actually returned an opinion on that entry. Using the roster size
as the denominator would let an entry reached by two auditors be decided on the same evidence as
one reached by four.

## Which fields are audited, and which are editorial

This distinction matters and is easy to lose.

**Audited.** The statement, why it is open, the prior work, and the extracted claims. These went
through literature verification, adversarial refutation and the independent auditors, and they
carry the verdict.

**Editorial.** Maturity, tractability, severity, the proposed research direction, and the
protocol-component and data-setting tags. These are one reader's judgment applied to make the
catalog browsable. They were not audited and should not be cited as findings. The proposed
direction in particular reads with the same visual authority as the audited statement above it,
and it is a research suggestion rather than a verified claim.

**Deliberately rebuilt.** Priority is not carried over from the source. It reflects three
observable things: whether the problem blocks a decision-grade estimand, whether any method
addresses it at all, and whether any software implements it.

## What the verdicts do not mean

A verdict is a judgment about a **claim**, not about a problem's importance.

[Overstated]{.verdict .verdict-overstated} almost never means the problem is fictional. It
usually means the underlying difficulty is real and the source pitched its severity, or the
claim that no method exists, more strongly than the evidence supports. The entry records the
strongest version of the claim that survived.

[Confirmed open]{.verdict .verdict-confirmed-open} means the checks agreed and no counterevidence
surfaced. It does not mean nobody is working on it, and it is a statement about the literature
that was reachable, not about the literature that exists.

[Unverifiable]{.verdict .verdict-unverifiable} means the auditors disagreed with evidence on both
sides, or that no accessible source could settle it. The disagreement is shown on the entry
rather than resolved silently.

## Limits of this exercise

**This is not a systematic review.** There was no protocol registration, no duplicate independent
screening with a reported agreement statistic, and no formal risk-of-bias assessment.

**The literature harvest covers PubMed and PubMed Central only.** Conference abstracts and
journals indexed in Embase but not PubMed are missing. Embase has no API available without a
subscription.

**The auditors are language models.** They are better at finding a paper that closes a gap than
at proving no such paper exists, so [Confirmed open]{.verdict .verdict-confirmed-open} carries
less weight than [Resolved since report]{.verdict .verdict-resolved-since-report}. A confirmed
absence of evidence is the weakest thing on this site.

## Reproducing this

Everything is in the repository. `build/render_site.mjs` turns the registry into these pages,
`build/make_audit_batches.mjs` produces the auditor prompts, and `build/adjudicate.mjs` applies
the rule. `documentation/audit/calibration.json` holds known-answer cases verified by hand; any
audit configuration that fails to reproduce them is miscalibrated, and they are asserted before
the site is built.
